**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, assignment).**

**What I found**
- **§ 16.2 (Assignment)** — the operative clause. Its opening sentence bars *either* Party from assigning without the other's prior written approval, with no affiliate or M&A carve-out for IBM and no reasonableness qualifier on the consent IBM must obtain. The reasonableness standard appears only for MSL's assignments to MSL Related Companies. This is the rule's stated walk-away case (blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out) and it also fails the fallback, which requires at minimum a mutual successor-assignment right on written notice.
- **§ 16.5 (Sale or Merger)** — favourable to us and left untouched: it binds MSL only, requiring immediate notice and assumption of performance by any successor. There is no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right running against IBM anywhere in the document (no "change of control" hits), so nothing needed deleting on that axis.
- **§ 16.7 (Assignees and Visits)** — a misnomer; it deals with IBM personnel on MSL premises, not assignment. No impact.
- **p1494** sits in an ancillary confidentiality exhibit, not the operative agreement, so I did not redline it.

**Redline (validated ok:true)** — a single replacement of the first sentence of § 16.2 that: (i) permits IBM to assign to a group company or to a successor by merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of substantially all relevant assets, on written notice; (ii) applies a not-unreasonably-withheld-or-delayed standard to the residual consent right; and (iii) confirms no such event gives MSL a termination, suspension or re-pricing right. MSL's own assignment restrictions and subcontractor-notice duty are preserved verbatim.
